entries.proposition: The comparison is treated real-world patients against untreated natural-history controls in one registry, matched 1:1 on baseline age within 12 months and exact baseline motor-language score.
entries.snippet: ERT-treated patients were matched 1:1 with untreated NH controls based on two criteria: baseline age (± 12 months) and baseline ML score (exact match).

entries.proposition: Treated data were collected prospectively while some control data were collected retrospectively.
entries.snippet: Data were prospectively collected from patients treated with cerliponase alfa between August 26, 2016 and December 31, 2020, while some data from untreated NH controls were collected retrospectively.
entries.anchor: Methods, Study design and data source

entries.proposition: The outcome is a disease-specific four-step ordinal scale scored by the treating physician at six-monthly visits; a score of 3 is normal and 0 is complete loss.
entries.snippet: Each domain on this scale measures loss of function, where a score of 3 indicates normal condition and a score of 0 represents complete loss of function

entries.proposition: Controls were followed only for as long as their matched treated patient (mean 76 weeks against 104 weeks).
entries.snippet: The mean (SD) follow-up time was 104.3 (63.9) weeks for the matched ERT-treated patients and 76.1 (43.1) for the matched NH control patients.

entries.proposition: Matching was balanced on age and score by construction (both 4.7 years and 3.9 points) but not on sex (52 percent female treated against 24 percent in controls).
entries.snippet: Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics were generally similar for the matched ERT-treated and NH control patients, apart from sex

entries.proposition: Time to an unreversed 2-point decline or a score of 0: hazard ratio 0.08 (interval 0.02 to 0.28); time to unreversed score of 0: 0.07 (0.01 to 0.40).
entries.snippet: ERT-treated patients were found to be significantly less likely to have an unreversed ML 2-point decline or score of 0 (hazard ratio [HR] 0.08; 95% confidence interval 0.02, 0.28; p < 0.0001)

entries.proposition: Rate of decline of the combined score: 0.46 points per 48 weeks treated against 1.88 in controls (difference 1.42, interval 0.74 to 2.10).
entries.snippet: with a mean (standard error) difference of 1.42 (0.33) (95% confidence interval 0.74, 2.10; p = 0.0003)

entries.proposition: Six of the 21 matched controls (29 percent) died over the equivalent follow-up and none of the treated patients did.
entries.snippet: No ERT-treated patients died during the follow-up period, whereas six NH patients (29%) in the matched cohort died over the equivalent period (median time to death: 313 weeks).

entries.proposition: The real-world effect size agrees with the pivotal trial: difference in decline rate 1.42 against 1.75 points, hazard ratios 0.08 and 0.07 against 0.14 and 0.02.
entries.snippet: mean difference in the rate of ML score decline per 48 weeks between ERT-treated patients and NH controls was similar to that reported in the clinical trials (mean difference: 1.42 vs. 1.75 points)

entries.proposition: In the five matched pairs with baseline score 2 or less, benefit appeared in three and not in two; the authors say further evidence is needed in advanced disease.
entries.snippet: The remaining two matched patients had no comparative benefit with cerliponase alfa on ML score decline.

entries.proposition: Among five patients treated before any decline (score 6), three kept a score of 6 for 7 to 10 months, but the authors note these children had not reached the age of expected decline.
entries.snippet: However, it should be noted that these patients had not reached the age at which the most significant decline would be expected based on the natural history of the classical CLN2 disease phenotype by the end of follow-up

entries.proposition: Stated limitations: no contemporaneous control (very few untreated patients exist since approval), residual confounding after matching, small sample (24), treatment-related adverse events only.
entries.snippet: the lack of a contemporaneous control group: since the approval of cerliponase alfa there have been very few untreated patients

entries.proposition: Supplement Table S2: in the full cohort the treated group had a later mean onset (3.4 against 2.9 years, p 0.02) and fewer motor-first presentations (17 against 42 percent, p 0.03) than controls, i.e. the overall groups differ before matching.
entries.snippet: Age at disease onset, years | Mean (SD) | n = 51 / 2.9 (0.8) | n = 23 / 3.4 (0.9) | 0.02

entries.proposition: Fig 1A: control curve reaches zero probability of no decline by about month 21 with a median near month 11 to 12, while the treated curve falls to about 0.47 at month 25 and then runs flat with 6 to 1 patients at risk; the flat tail carries censoring ticks and is not a measured step.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 1A KM time to unreversed 2-point decline or score 0: NH dashed falls from 1.0 at month about 4 to 0.29 at month 12 and 0 at month about 21; ERT solid 0.95 at month 6, 0.89 at 11, 0.84 at 14, 0.56 at 19.5, 0.47 from month 25 to 51; at risk ERT 21,21,18,17,16,11,9,6,6,4,3,3,3,3,3,2,2,1 and NH 21,21,19,11,8,5,4,1.

entries.proposition: Fig 1B: unreversed score of 0 occurs in controls from month 10 to 30 (0 probability at month 30 with 1 at risk) and in the treated group in one patient at month about 25 (curve 0.85 thereafter).
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 1B KM time to unreversed score 0: NH falls from 1.0 at month 10 to 0.71 at 12, 0.53 at 14, 0.38 at 19, 0.29 at 22, 0.19 at 24, 0 at 30; ERT 0.95 at month 6 and 0.85 from month 25.

entries.proposition: NOT WWOX EVIDENCE (CLN2 disease, enzyme replacement versus natural history). In the three-criteria sensitivity analysis (matched on baseline age, exact baseline score and genotype, 18 pairs) the rate of decline was 0.49 points per 48 weeks treated against 2.07 in controls, a difference of 1.58 (interval 0.76 to 2.40).

Even in the three-criteria matched set the treated group had a later mean onset than controls (3.4 against 2.9 years, P = 0.06) and more often first presented with seizures (89 against 61 percent, P = 0.05), so onset age and presenting symptom were not balanced by matching on age, score and genotype.
entries.snippet: Age at disease onset, years Mean (SD) n = 17 / 2.9 (0.8) n = 17 / 3.4 (0.8) 0.06

entries.proposition: The sensitivity-analysis matching is stated as baseline age within 12 months, exact baseline score and genotype (0, 1 or 2 common alleles).
entries.snippet: Patients matched based on baseline age (± 12 months), baseline ML score (exact match), and genotype (0, 1, or 2 common alleles).
